h: Tips for Taking On the Tech
p: If you've never played the techy version of these old pub games, there's a small learning curve, but it's a fun one. The augmented-reality set-up projects targets and scores onto the boards, which means you can pick game modes that are a world away from the traditional 501. Some formats suit beginners and kids brilliantly, because luck and a steady hand count as much as years of practice down the local.

For darts, stand comfortably, keep your elbow still and let the wrist do the work. For shuffleboard, it's all about touch rather than power: the cheeky pucks have a habit of sailing off the end if you shove too hard, and the clever play is often knocking your rival's puck out of the way rather than racing for the top score. Expect at least one family member to discover a hidden talent and refuse to stop talking about it.

Clacton Pier has been part of the seafront since 1871, and once you've finished your games it's well worth stepping off and exploring a bit further. The seafront gardens along the clifftop are lovely for a stroll, and the long sandy beaches with their neat lines of beach huts stretch towards Holland-on-Sea in one direction and Jaywick in the other.

A short drive up the coast takes you to genteel Frinton-on-Sea, with its wide greensward and grand houses, and then Walton-on-the-Naze, where the Naze Tower stands on crumbling cliffs famous for fossil-hunting. It's a stretch of the Essex Sunshine Coast that suits families who like a mix of buzz and breathing space.
